title: De praedestinatione: title — Rom 9:18 and Calvin
pass_a_gloss: DISSERTATION ON PREDESTINATION AND REPROBATION. By the Most Reverend man John Davenant, lately Bishop of Salisbury, some years earlier Professor of Theology in the most celebrated University of Cambridge, dictated in the Theological Schools to his hearers. Romans 9:18. Of whom he wills, he has mercy: and whom he wills, he hardens. Calvin on Romans 9:18. There is least doubt that Paul speaks these things from his own sense, namely that God BY HIS OWN ARBITRARY WILL deigns with mercy whom it has seemed good to him; against whomever it has pleased he draws tight the severity of judgment. From the workshop of Roger Daniel, Printer of the nurturing University of Cambridge, 1650.
pass_b_english: A DISSERTATION ON PREDESTINATION AND REPROBATION. By the Most Reverend John Davenant, lately Bishop of Salisbury, formerly Professor of Theology in the University of Cambridge, delivered in the Theological Schools to his hearers. [[Romans 9:18 >> Bible:Romans 9:18]]. Of whom he wills, he has mercy; and whom he wills, he hardens. Calvin on Romans 9:18: There is scarcely any doubt that Paul speaks here in his own sense — that God, by his own free decision, shows mercy to whom he chooses, and draws the severity of judgment against whomever he pleases. Printed at Cambridge by Roger Daniel, University Printer, 1650.
source_text: DISSERTATIO DE PRAEDESTINATIONE ET REPROBATIONE. Per Reverendissimum virum JOANNEM DAVENANTIUM, Nuper Episcopum SARISBURIENSEM, Ante aliquot annos in celeberrima Academia Cantabrigiensi Theologiae Professorem in Scholis Theologicis auditoribus suis dictata. Rom. IX. 18. Cujus vult, miseretur: & quem vult, indurat. Calvin. in Rom. IX. 18. Minime dubium est, Paulum e suo ipsius sensu haec loqui, Deum scilicet PRO ARBITRIO SUO, quem visum illi fuerit, misericordia dignari: in quemcunque libuerit judicii severitatem stringere. Ex Officina Rogeri Danielis, Alma Academiae Cantabrigiensis Typographi, 1650.
